History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Um, I've got this thing when I pee, and it hurts when I go to the loo, and I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out.
Patient: I've got, pain in my tummy.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Abdominal pain is located in the lower abdomen.
Abdominal pain is in the midline.
Abdominal pain severity is 7 out of 10.
Patient is able to pass urine.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: OK. And have you actually been able to pass water OK? Patient: Yes, but I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots.

History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: And, have you had these symptoms before? Patient: No.

Doctor: Two hundred milligrams? Patient: Yes.

Medications.source_text: Doctor: OK. And it, do you take it three times a day? Patient: Yes I do.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Consumes about one glass of wine per week.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Patient: One glass of wine a week.
Doctor: OK. And do you smoke? Patient: No.
Doctor: No. Do you have regular periods? Patient: Yes I do.

Assessment.content: Clinical impression is a urinary tract infection.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: OK. Um, it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine.

Plan_of_Care.content: Obtain a thermometer from the pharmacy and monitor temperature at home.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: OK. It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature, just to make sure that it isn't, going up and down.

Plan_of_Care.content: Treat empirically without urine testing using a course of antibiotics.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Um, normally we can treat this infection without having to test your urine. Uh, with, with a course of antibiotics.

Plan_of_Care.content: Antibiotic course duration is three days.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: It would just be for three days.

Plan_of_Care.content: Send prescription to the requested pharmacy; patient to pick up and start antibiotics as soon as possible.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Yes, so I can send a prescription through to your requested pharmacy for that. If you take them, as soon as you can, get them, pick them up as soon as you can, and start taking them.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase fluid intake to approximately 2.5 to 3 litres of water daily.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: The other thing which is important to do is to drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day.

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider drinking cranberry juice as adjunctive therapy.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Um, you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well, that sometimes helps.

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider over-the-counter urinary alkalinising sachets from the chemist.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And also some, sachets um, which you can get from the chemist, some sachets which just help change the acidity of your urine.

Follow_up_Information.content: Seek medical review if pain worsens or does not settle, if lower back pain develops, if a high temperature occurs, or if there are problems passing urine.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: Um, if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again.

Follow_up_Information.content: If symptoms become recurrent, further discussion with a clinician is advised.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: Um, the other thing is that if it becomes a, common, thing or a recurrent problem. Then we need to talk to you again about it.

Follow_up_Information.content: No need to call after finishing antibiotics if symptoms have resolved.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Patient: So, do I have to call after I finish my course of antibiotics. Doctor: No, not if you're better.
